question.text: Some historians believe this tsar lost his sanity when his wife died in 1560. His son Feodor's unsuccessful reign led to the Time of Troubles.
question.clue: This man's epithet likely comes from his violent subjugation of the boyars.

swap.leadin: This monarch put down Pugachev's Rebellion, and her lover Grigory Orlov helped orchestrate a coup to overthrow her husband, Peter III.
swap.text: Name this empress of Russia known as "the Great."
swap.answerHtml: Catherine the Great [or Catherine II; or Yekaterina Velikaya; or Yekaterina Alekseevna; or Princess Sophie of Anhalt-Zerbst]
swap.clue: Victories at the Chesma, Iasi, and Ochakov led to favorable terms in the Treaty of Jassy that expanded this ruler's empire.

question.leadin: This leader's policy of perestroika, or "restructuring," attempted to keep his country alive into the 21st century. It didn't.
question.text: Name this leader asked by Ronald Reagan to "tear down this wall." He was succeeded by Boris Yeltsin during the collapse of the Soviet Union.
question.clue: This leader, who described his diplomacy with the "Sinatra Doctrine," appointed Eduard Shevardnadze as his Minister of Foreign Affairs and succeeded Constantin Chernenko.

swap.leadin: In the late 17th century, this ruler went on a Grand Embassy of Europe, exploring methods to Westernize his country.
swap.text: Name this "Great" member of the Romanov dynasty.
swap.clue: He created the table of ranks and required lifetime service from the nobility while defeating Sweden in the Great Northern War.

question.leadin: One work about this event was later banned in the Soviet Union for emphasizing Leon Trotsky's role and devaluing Joseph Stalin's role in this event.
question.text: Name this event which featured an assault on the Winter Palace. This late 1917 event resulted in the dissolution of Alexander Kerensky's provisional government and the later establishment of the Soviet Union.
question.answerHtml: October Revolution [or Bolshevik Revolution; or Red October; accept synonyms for revolution such as coup; prompt on Russian Revolution]
question.clue: Alexander Kerensky's cadets in Petrograd failed to hold the Winter Palace near the beginning of this event.

swap.leadin: The nurse Darya Mikhailova ("mih-HAIL-oh-vuh") took care of Russian soldiers from this war wounded at the Battle of Alma.
swap.text: Name this 1853-1856 war, during which Sevastopol ("seh-VAST-oh-pull") was besieged for eleven months. A group of 38 nurses worked at the Scutari Barracks during this war.
swap.clue: This war began after one side issued an ultimatum that asserted its right to protect foreign Christians.

question.text: This Grand Prince of Kiev married the sister of the Byzantine Emperor Basil II and famously converted to Christianity after rejecting Islam for its ban on alcohol and pork.
question.answerHtml: Vladimir the Great [accept Saint Vladimir; accept Vladimir Sviatoslavich; prompt on Vladimir]
question.clue: In 988, this father of Yaroslav the Wise married Anna Porphyrogenita ], the sister of Basil the Bulgar Slayer, confirming an alliance with the Byzantines and formalizing this man's conversion to Christianity.

swap.text: The war effectively came to an end after the Malakoff Redoubt was captured in a siege of this most populous city on the Crimean Peninsula.
swap.clue: William Howard Russell coined a name for troops who fought off an attack on this city by General Liprandi.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a historical figure.
question.text: Mazepa served as the hetman of these fiercely independent horsemen who lived along the Don river and often served in the Czar's armies.
question.clue: A series of military campaigns in Poland called the "Deluge" occurred following an uprising of these people led by Bogdan Khmelnytsky ("k'mel-NIT-skee").

swap.leadin: Identify these uppity groups from Russian history.
swap.text: Beginning as the political wing of the Land and Liberty movement, this group agitated for sweeping reforms, most of which Alexander II was pursuing when they bombed him to death, leading them to be harshly targeted in incidents like the Trial of Fourteen under Alexander III.
swap.clue: Sophia Perovskaya was the first woman executed for terrorism after she led this organization in an action where Nikolai Rysakov and Ignacy Hrenieweisky threw bombs at a carriage.

question.leadin: Wikipedia notes this man's famous zinger "No Dream" was addressed to the Poles.
question.text: Name this Russian tsar from 1855 to 1881, who was responsible for instituting the zemstvo system and ending the Crimean War.
question.clue: This Romanov who ruled Russia from 1855 until 1881, the second of his name.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about reforms in Russia under Alexander II.
swap.text: In 1861, Alexander II issued legislation emancipating these people, who had previously been bound to their masters' land. However, these people still had to pay forty-nine "redemption payments" after their freedom.
swap.clue: Many of these people moved into communes called mir after being granted land in the Pauper's Allotment.

question.leadin: The October Manifesto, a guarantee of reforms drafted following the 1905 Revolution, promised to create this legislative body.
question.text: Name this legislative body that served as the lower house of the parliament of the Russian Empire, under the State Council. It shares its name with the lower house of the modern Russian Federation's Federal Assembly.
question.clue: Alexis Aldadin formed the Trudoviks to stand for election to this body.

swap.leadin: These people were killed after they participated in the Bezdna Unrest.
swap.text: Identify this class of people who were freed by an 1861 decree during the reign of Alexander II.
swap.clue: An imperial edict by Paul I forbade compelling these people to perform corvee labor on Sundays.

question.leadin: This philosopher declared that "The revolutionist is a doomed man" in a tract he wrote with Sergey Nechayev, Catechism of a Revolutionist.
question.text: Name this philosopher who outlined his beliefs in works such as Statism and Anarchy. Due to his feuds with Karl Marx, this philosopher was expelled from the International Workingmen's Association in 1872.
question.clue: His quarrel with Marx at the First International split the European communist movement. He argued for the education of the common man in an effort to enable society to rise up and destroy most institutions. For 15 points-name this author of God and the State, the chief propagator of nineteenth-century anarchism.

swap.text: The capture of this city was part of Operation Edelweiss. This city now called Volgograd was the site of a battle that was the turning point of the Eastern Front of World War II and ended in the capture of German Field Marshal Friedrich Paulus.
swap.clue: In a battle for this city, Operation Uranus resulted in the encirclement of the German Sixth Army under field marshal Friedrich Paulus, which Adolf Hitler then ordered to be supplied from the air.

question.leadin: Lavrenty Beria investigated this man for packing seven rail carriages full of German valuables in the Trophy Affair, an affront this man repaid by helping convict Beria of treason.
question.text: Name this decorated general who defeated the Kwantung Army early in his career at the Battle of Khalkhin Gol, and then directed the occupation of Bessarabia.
question.clue: This general assisted a future premier in arresting his rival Lavrentiy Beria.

swap.leadin: This namesake of a class of icebreaker ships is attested in the charter of Kostroma, which was partially given to his son-in-law Bogdan in tribute to this man's deeds.
swap.text: Name this legendary figure, who is said to have led a Polish army looking for the Hypatian Monastery into death in the deep woods instead.

question.leadin: This president lost popularity after censoring media coverage concerning his negotiations over the disputed Tuzla Island.
question.text: Give this president who pursued a dual policy of appeasing the West and Russia, known as his Multi-Vector Doctrine. This man's downfall ultimately occurred due his involvement in the assassination of journalistGeorgiy Gongadze.

swap.text: In this revolution, demonstrators forced the resignation of Eduard Shevardnadze, and Mikhail Saakashvili won the election that followed to become the president of Georgia.
swap.clue: James Baker attempted to prevent this event by developing an electoral formula, which was subsequently ignored.
